# 12-Week Strength + Hypertrophy Programme

**Client:** 26F, recreational lifter, COC-controlled (no cycle phasing required), fully cleared for full intensity
**Programme Start:** Monday, 2026-06-01
**Programme End:** Sunday, 2026-08-23
**Structure:** 4 sessions/week — Upper/Lower split with strength bias on Days 1 & 3, hypertrophy bias on Days 2 & 4
**Default Schedule:** Mon (Lower Strength) / Tue (Upper Strength) / Thu (Lower Hypertrophy) / Fri (Upper Hypertrophy)

Because there is no menstrual cycle to programme around, loading, deload placement, and high-intensity sessions can be distributed purely on training logic. The programme follows a standard three-block structure: Accumulation → Intensification → Realisation, with a deload in Week 4, Week 8, and a taper in Week 12.

---

## PHASE 1 — ACCUMULATION (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Build work capacity, refine technique, accumulate hypertrophic volume.
**Strength sets:** 4×6 @ RPE 7 → progressing to RPE 8
**Hypertrophy sets:** 3–4×10–12 @ RPE 7–8
**Rest:** 2–3 min compounds, 60–90 s accessories

### Week 1 (Jun 1 – Jun 7) — Introduction

**Day 1 — Lower Strength (Mon)**
- Back squat — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Romanian deadlift — 3×8 @ RPE 7
- Walking lunge — 3×10/leg
- Leg press — 3×12
- Standing calf raise — 4×12
- Hanging knee raise — 3×12

**Day 2 — Upper Strength (Tue)**
- Bench press — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Pendlay row — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Seated DB shoulder press — 3×8
- Lat pulldown — 3×10
- DB lateral raise — 3×12
- Cable triceps pressdown — 3×12

**Day 3 — Lower Hypertrophy (Thu)**
- Front squat — 3×8 @ RPE 7
- Hip thrust — 4×10
- Bulgarian split squat — 3×10/leg
- Lying hamstring curl — 3×12
- Seated calf raise — 4×15
- Cable woodchop — 3×12/side

**Day 4 — Upper Hypertrophy (Fri)**
- Incline DB bench press — 4×10
- Chest-supported row — 4×10
- Arnold press — 3×12
- Cable face pull — 3×15
- EZ-bar curl — 3×12
- Overhead triceps extension — 3×12

### Week 2 (Jun 8 – Jun 14) — Add a rep/load
Same template; add 2.5–5 kg on main lifts or +1 rep where RPE allows. Strength work moves toward RPE 7.5.

### Week 3 (Jun 15 – Jun 21) — Peak accumulation
Strength lifts: 4×6 @ RPE 8. Hypertrophy sets pushed to RPE 8–8.5. Add one extra set to one accessory per body part.

### Week 4 (Jun 22 – Jun 28) — Deload
- All loads at ~65% of Week 3 working weight
- Sets reduced by ~40% (e.g., 4×6 becomes 2×6)
- Keep movement quality high; no failure work
- Add 1–2 mobility/easy cardio sessions (20–30 min Z2)

---

## PHASE 2 — INTENSIFICATION (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** Shift toward heavier loads while maintaining hypertrophy volume on Days 2 & 4.
**Strength sets:** 5×4 @ RPE 7.5 → RPE 8.5
**Hypertrophy sets:** 3–4×8–10 @ RPE 8

### Week 5 (Jun 29 – Jul 5) — Reintroduction

**Day 1 — Lower Strength**
- Back squat — 5×4 @ RPE 7.5
- Conventional deadlift — 4×5 @ RPE 7.5
- Reverse lunge — 3×8/leg
- Leg press — 3×10
- Standing calf raise — 4×10
- Cable crunch — 3×12

**Day 2 — Upper Strength**
- Bench press — 5×4 @ RPE 7.5
- Weighted pull-up (or lat pulldown) — 4×5
- Standing overhead press — 4×6
- Seated cable row — 3×10
- DB lateral raise — 4×12
- Close-grip bench press — 3×8

**Day 3 — Lower Hypertrophy**
- Front squat — 3×6 @ RPE 8
- Hip thrust — 4×8
- Bulgarian split squat — 3×8/leg
- Seated hamstring curl — 4×10
- Seated calf raise — 4×12
- Hanging leg raise — 3×10

**Day 4 — Upper Hypertrophy**
- Incline barbell bench — 4×8
- One-arm DB row — 4×8/side
- DB shoulder press — 3×10
- Cable face pull — 3×15
- Incline DB curl — 3×10
- Cable triceps pressdown — 3×12

### Week 6 (Jul 6 – Jul 12)
Add load on main lifts. Strength RPE 8. Hypertrophy: +1 set on one lagging movement.

### Week 7 (Jul 13 – Jul 19) — Peak intensification
Strength lifts: 5×4 @ RPE 8.5. Final hypertrophy push — accessories to RPE 8.5–9.

### Week 8 (Jul 20 – Jul 26) — Deload
Same protocol as Week 4. Test movement quality, sleep, soreness. Optional: light technique work on competition lifts at 60–70% to refine bar path.

---

## PHASE 3 — REALISATION (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** Express strength on main lifts while preserving lean mass; taper into Week 12.
**Strength sets:** Move toward heavier triples and doubles.
**Hypertrophy sets:** Reduce volume by ~20%, maintain intensity.

### Week 9 (Jul 27 – Aug 2)

**Day 1 — Lower Strength**
- Back squat — 4×3 @ RPE 8
- Conventional deadlift — 3×3 @ RPE 8
- Walking lunge — 3×8/leg
- Leg press — 3×10
- Standing calf raise — 3×10
- Hanging knee raise — 3×10

**Day 2 — Upper Strength**
- Bench press — 4×3 @ RPE 8
- Weighted pull-up — 4×4
- Push press — 3×5
- Chest-supported row — 3×8
- DB lateral raise — 3×12
- Close-grip bench — 3×6

**Day 3 — Lower Hypertrophy** (volume reduced)
- Front squat — 3×5
- Hip thrust — 3×8
- Bulgarian split squat — 3×8/leg
- Lying hamstring curl — 3×10
- Seated calf raise — 3×12

**Day 4 — Upper Hypertrophy** (volume reduced)
- Incline DB press — 3×8
- One-arm DB row — 3×8/side
- Arnold press — 3×10
- Face pull — 3×15
- EZ curl — 3×10
- Overhead triceps — 3×10

### Week 10 (Aug 3 – Aug 9)
Strength lifts: 4×3 @ RPE 8.5. Add small loads where bar speed remains crisp.

### Week 11 (Aug 10 – Aug 16) — Peak week
- Back squat — 3×2 @ RPE 9
- Bench press — 3×2 @ RPE 9
- Deadlift — 2×2 @ RPE 9
- Overhead press — 3×3 @ RPE 8.5
- Accessories trimmed to 2–3 sets; no failure work.

### Week 12 (Aug 17 – Aug 23) — Taper / Test Week
**Mon — Lower test**
- Back squat — work up to a heavy 3RM or 1RM (trainer's call based on goal)
- Deadlift — heavy 3RM or 1RM
- 1–2 easy accessory movements

**Tue — Upper test**
- Bench press — heavy 3RM or 1RM
- Overhead press — 3×5 @ moderate load
- Pull-ups — 3×AMRAP

**Thu/Fri — Optional light pump session or rest**
Then reassess and begin Block 2 the following week.

---

## Recovery & Lifestyle Notes

- **Sleep:** Target 7.5–9 hrs/night. Flag any week where average drops below 7.
- **Steps:** Maintain 8–10k daily as baseline NEAT.
- **Conditioning:** 1–2× weekly low-intensity Z2 (20–40 min) on non-lifting days. Optional 1× short interval session in Weeks 1–10, removed in Weeks 11–12.
- **Warm-up:** 5 min general (bike/row) + 2–3 movement-specific ramp sets.
- **Mobility:** 5–10 min targeted post-session (hips, t-spine, ankles).
- **Tracking:** Log loads, RPE, bodyweight (weekly average), and a simple readiness score (1–10) at session start.

## Nutrition Framework (general — adjust to client goal)

- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg bodyweight daily, spread across 3–5 meals.
- **Carbs:** Prioritise around training (pre- and post-session). 3–5 g/kg on training days depending on goal.
- **Fats:** 0.8–1.0 g/kg minimum for hormonal health.
- **Hydration:** 30–35 ml/kg + 500 ml per training hour.
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 5 g/day, any time.
- **Caffeine:** Optional 3–5 mg/kg pre-session; cap 6+ hours before bed.
- **Calorie target:** Depends on goal — confirm whether this is a recomp, lean gain, or maintenance block. The programme works under any of these; bias toward a slight surplus (+150–250 kcal) if hypertrophy is the priority.

## Progression Rules

- If all prescribed reps are completed at the target RPE with one rep in reserve, add 2.5 kg upper / 5 kg lower next session.
- If RPE exceeds target by >1 for two consecutive sessions, hold load and chase technique.
- Replace any exercise causing joint irritation with a similar pattern (e.g., front squat ↔ safety bar squat, conventional ↔ trap bar deadlift).

Let me know if you'd like me to swap the split (e.g., to PPL or full body), bias the programme toward a specific goal (powerlifting peak vs. physique), or adjust the testing protocol in Week 12.

# Nutrition Plan — Hypertrophy Support

**Client:** 26F recreational lifter, 4 lifting sessions/week + light conditioning
**Goal:** Support hypertrophy and strength gains across the 12-week block
**Approach:** Slight, sustained calorie surplus with high protein, periodised carbs around training, and a structured weekly check-in

Because exact bodyweight wasn't provided, I've built this around a working example of **65 kg** — scale the absolute numbers to the client's actual weight using the per-kg targets given.

---

## 1. Calorie Target

**Estimated maintenance:** ~2,100–2,300 kcal/day (sedentary BMR ~1,400 + training and NEAT)

**Lean gain surplus:** +200–300 kcal/day above maintenance
**Working target:** **~2,400–2,500 kcal/day**

Expected rate of gain: **0.25–0.4 kg/week** (≈1–1.5 kg over the 12 weeks). Faster than this and fat gain outpaces muscle gain in a trained recreational lifter; slower and progress on the bar stalls.

---

## 2. Macronutrient Targets

For a 65 kg client at ~2,450 kcal:

| Macro | Per kg BW | Grams/day | Calories | % of total |
|-------|-----------|-----------|----------|------------|
| Protein | 2.0 g/kg | 130 g | 520 | ~21% |
| Carbohydrate | 5.0 g/kg | 325 g | 1,300 | ~53% |
| Fat | 1.0 g/kg | 65 g | 585 | ~24% |
| Fibre | — | 28–35 g | — | — |

**Per-kg rules to scale up or down:**
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg on training days, 3–4 g/kg on rest days
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg (floor for hormonal health and satiety)

**Training vs. rest day split (optional refinement):**
- Training days: ~2,500 kcal (carbs at the upper end)
- Rest days: ~2,300 kcal (carbs down ~50 g, fat up ~10 g)

---

## 3. Meal Structure

Four meals + one intra/post-training snack works well for protein distribution (aim for **30–40 g protein per meal** to maximise muscle protein synthesis across the day).

**Sample training day (~2,500 kcal):**

| Meal | Time | Example | Protein | Carbs | Fat |
|------|------|---------|---------|-------|-----|
| Breakfast | 07:30 | 3 eggs, 80 g oats, 200 ml milk, berries, 1 tbsp peanut butter | 35 g | 70 g | 22 g |
| Lunch | 12:30 | 150 g chicken breast, 250 g cooked rice, mixed veg, olive oil | 45 g | 85 g | 15 g |
| Pre-training snack | 16:30 | Greek yoghurt 200 g, banana, honey | 20 g | 50 g | 3 g |
| Post-training shake | 18:30 | Whey 30 g + 30 g dextrose/oats | 25 g | 30 g | 2 g |
| Dinner | 20:00 | 150 g salmon, 300 g potato, salad, 1 tbsp olive oil | 35 g | 60 g | 25 g |

**Totals:** ~160 g protein / 295 g carbs / 67 g fat / ~2,500 kcal
*(Slightly over protein target — fine; trim portions if you want it tighter.)*

**Rest day adjustment:** Drop the pre-training snack and post-training shake; add a fourth meal of similar size to lunch with lower carbs.

---

## 4. Nutrient Timing

- **Pre-training (60–120 min before):** 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein. Improves session quality and reduces muscle protein breakdown.
- **Post-training (within 1–2 hrs):** 30–40 g protein + 50–80 g carbs. Replenishes glycogen and drives MPS.
- **Protein distribution:** Aim for ~0.4 g/kg per meal across 4–5 feedings, with the largest dose in the meal closest to training.
- **Pre-bed:** A slow-digesting protein source (cottage cheese, casein shake, Greek yoghurt) ~30 g supports overnight recovery.

---

## 5. Hydration

- **Baseline:** 30–35 ml/kg → **~2.2 L/day** for 65 kg
- **Training:** +500–750 ml per training hour
- **Electrolytes:** 1–2 g sodium added to water on heavy training days, especially if she sweats heavily or trains in warm conditions
- Practical check: pale-straw urine, no afternoon energy crashes

---

## 6. Supplements (evidence-based, hypertrophy-supportive)

| Supplement | Dose | When | Purpose |
|------------|------|------|---------|
| Creatine monohydrate | 5 g/day | Any time, daily (including rest days) | Strength, work capacity, hypertrophy |
| Whey protein | 25–40 g/serving | As needed to hit protein target | Convenience |
| Vitamin D3 | 1,000–2,000 IU/day | With a meal containing fat | Common deficiency in women; bone & hormonal health |
| Omega-3 (EPA+DHA) | 2 g/day | With a meal | Recovery, joint, anti-inflammatory |
| Caffeine (optional) | 3–5 mg/kg | 30–45 min pre-training | Performance |
| Magnesium glycinate (optional) | 200–400 mg | Evening | Sleep, muscle relaxation |

**COC-specific note:** Combined oral contraceptives can slightly increase requirements for B6, B12, folate, magnesium, and zinc. A standard women's multivitamin covers this comfortably — worth including as insurance rather than chasing individual micronutrients.

---

## 7. Phase-Specific Tweaks

The macros above carry the client through most of the block. Two small adjustments line up with the programme phases:

**Weeks 1–8 (Accumulation + Intensification):**
- Full surplus (+250 kcal)
- Carbs at the top of the range on training days
- This is where the bulk of lean tissue gain happens

**Weeks 9–11 (Realisation):**
- Maintain surplus; do not cut here, even though hypertrophy volume drops
- Carbs stay high — heavy strength work is glycogen-dependent
- Protein non-negotiable

**Week 12 (Taper/Test week):**
- Drop to maintenance (~2,250 kcal) — training volume is much lower
- Keep carbs high the day before and morning of testing sessions
- Salt food normally; hydrate well; avoid novel foods or alcohol in the 48 hrs pre-test

**Deload weeks (4 and 8):**
- No calorie change needed — short deloads don't warrant it
- Useful window to address GI issues, sleep, or any habits that have slipped

---

## 8. Weekly Monitoring

Track these on Sunday mornings before the week starts:

1. **Bodyweight:** Daily on waking, post-toilet, before food/water. Use the **7-day average**, not single readings.
2. **Weekly average change:** Target +0.15 to +0.35% of bodyweight/week (≈100–250 g for this client).
3. **Waist circumference:** At navel, weekly. Should rise much more slowly than bodyweight.
4. **Progress photos:** Front, side, back, same lighting, every 2 weeks.
5. **Training logs:** Are loads and reps progressing as programmed? This is the single best indicator of whether nutrition is dialled in.

**Decision rules:**
- Gaining >0.4 kg/week for 2 consecutive weeks → drop calories by 150 kcal (cut carbs)
- Gaining <0.1 kg/week for 2 consecutive weeks AND training is progressing → add 150 kcal (add carbs)
- Training stalling AND weight flat → add 200 kcal
- Waist rising disproportionately to weight → hold calories, audit food quality and sleep

---

## 9. Food Quality & Practical Notes

- **80/20 rule:** ~80% of intake from whole, minimally processed sources; 20% flexible. This is a sustainability decision, not a moral one.
- **Protein anchors:** Chicken, lean beef, fish, eggs, Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, whey, tofu, tempeh. Build each meal around one.
- **Carb anchors:** Rice, oats, potatoes, pasta, bread, fruit. Don't fear them — this client is training hard and needs them.
- **Fat sources:** Olive oil, avocado, nuts, oily fish, whole eggs, full-fat dairy. Easy to over-consume — measure oils.
- **Veg/fruit:** Minimum 3 servings veg + 2 fruit daily for micronutrients and fibre.
- **Alcohol:** Not banned, but blunts MPS and recovery. Cap at ~3 drinks/week, not on training days.

---

Let me know the client's actual bodyweight, dietary preferences (omnivore/vegetarian/etc.), allergies, and any logistical constraints (work schedule, cooking ability) and I'll convert this into a fully prescribed meal plan with exact grams.

# Cardio Addition — General Health Focus

**Goal:** Cover the cardiovascular, metabolic, and longevity benefits of aerobic training **without compromising hypertrophy or strength progress**.
**Approach:** Low-to-moderate volume, mostly Zone 2, with a small dose of higher-intensity work. Placed to minimise interference with lifting.

---

## 1. Weekly Cardio Targets

Aligned with general health guidelines (WHO, ACSM) and tuned for a lifter prioritising hypertrophy:

| Modality | Weekly volume | Intensity | Purpose |
|----------|---------------|-----------|---------|
| Zone 2 (steady) | 2 × 30–40 min | RPE 3–4 / "conversational" / ~60–70% HRmax | Aerobic base, recovery, metabolic health |

**Total structured cardio:** ~80–100 min/week. This is enough to drive meaningful health adaptations and stay well clear of the volume threshold where aerobic work begins to interfere with strength and hypertrophy.

## 2. Zone 2 Definition (practical)

- **Talk test:** Can hold a conversation in full sentences, but wouldn't want to sing.
- **Heart rate:** Roughly 60–70% of HRmax. For a 26F, that's ~120–140 bpm (rough estimate; refine with actual data).
- **RPE:** 3–4/10.
- **Modalities:** Brisk walking on incline, easy cycling, easy rowing, cross-trainer, swimming. **Avoid running** as the default — its eccentric load adds recovery cost on top of the lifting block.

## 3. Higher-Intensity Session Options

Pick one format per week. Rotate every 3–4 weeks for variety.

- 6 × 1 min hard (RPE 8) / 2 min easy
- 5 min cool-down
- Total: ~28 min

**Option B — Rower intervals**
- 5 min warm-up
- 4 × 500 m hard / 2 min easy
- 5 min cool-down
- Total: ~25 min

**Option C — Incline treadmill walk/jog**
- 5 min warm-up
- 8 × 30 sec hard / 90 sec easy
- 5 min cool-down
- Total: ~24 min

**Option D (later in block) — Norwegian-style 4×4**
- 5 min warm-up
- 4 × 4 min @ RPE 8 / 3 min easy
- 5 min cool-down
- Total: ~38 min — high-yield but high cost; use sparingly

## 4. Weekly Placement

Training week recap:
- **Mon:** Lower Strength
- **Tue:** Upper Strength
- **Wed:** Off
- **Thu:** Lower Hypertrophy
- **Fri:** Upper Hypertrophy
- **Sat:** Off
- **Sun:** Off

| Tue | Upper Strength | Z2 30 min (PM, ≥6 hr after lifting) | Optional; cycle or incline walk |
| Wed | Off | **Intervals 20–25 min** | Fully recovered, fully separated from lifting |
| Thu | Lower Hypertrophy | — | Protect lower-body recovery |
| Fri | Upper Hypertrophy | Z2 30 min (PM) | Optional; non-impact |
| Sat | Off | **Z2 40 min** | Outdoor walk/hike/easy ride |

**Key rules:**
1. **Never place Z2 or intervals immediately before a lower-body lifting session.** Minimum 24 hours separation.
2. **Separate cardio and lifting on the same day by ≥6 hours** when possible. If not possible, lift first, cardio after.
3. **No high-intensity cardio on Mon, Tue, Thu, or Fri.** It compounds neural fatigue and dampens the strength sessions.
4. **Use non-impact modalities** (bike, row, incline walk) on Sat to avoid loading legs before the next training week.

## 5. Phase-Specific Adjustments

The cardio dose tracks the demands of each phase:

**Phase 1 — Accumulation (Weeks 1–4):**
- Full prescription: 2× Z2 + 1× intervals + Sat Z2
- Lifting volume is moderate; cardio can be at the upper end

**Phase 2 — Intensification (Weeks 5–8):**
- Maintain Z2 sessions
- Reduce intervals to 1× every 7–10 days OR shorten work intervals
- Heavier strength work needs more neural recovery

**Phase 3 — Realisation (Weeks 9–11):**
- Drop intervals entirely
- Keep 1–2× Z2 30 min/week for circulation and recovery
- Daily steps continue

**Week 12 — Taper/Test:**
- Cardio off Mon–Wed (testing days)
- Easy Z2 walk only post-testing
- Resume normal cardio the following week

**Deload weeks (4 and 8):**
- This is actually a good time to **add** a Z2 session, not cut one — low-intensity aerobic work aids recovery
- Skip intervals during deloads

## 6. Monitoring

Add two simple metrics to the existing weekly check-in:

1. **Resting heart rate (morning, on waking):** Should trend down or stay stable over the block. A sustained rise of >5 bpm flags accumulated fatigue.
2. **Z2 pace/power at fixed HR:** For example, watts on the bike at 130 bpm. Should drift upward over weeks — that's the aerobic base improving.

If a wearable is available, **time in Zone 2** is a useful weekly target (aim ~60–80 min). If not, the talk test is fine.

---

## 7. Practical Notes

- **Warm-up for intervals:** Don't skip the 5-min ramp. Cold high-intensity work is where most cardio injuries happen.
- **Fasted Z2 is fine** for the AM walker; intervals should be fuelled (some carbs 60–90 min prior).
- **Add ~100–150 kcal on harder cardio days** if appetite allows — the surplus target assumed lifting only, and the intervals + Sat Z2 add meaningful expenditure.
- **Hot weather:** Cap intervals or move them indoors; heat stress compounds training stress quickly.
- **If she enjoys a specific modality** (spin class, swimming, hiking, padel, etc.), substitute it for the Sat Z2 — adherence beats optimality. Just keep the intensity honest.

## Monitoring Flags Specific to This Push

Higher intensity earns higher returns but tightens the margin for error. Watch for:

2. **Morning resting HR.** A sustained +5 bpm rise over baseline for 3+ days = pull back the next session by one set on main lifts.

# Adding a HIIT Day — Phase 2 Revised

A dedicated HIIT day adds a meaningful cardiovascular and metabolic stimulus, but it's not free — especially layered on top of the higher-intensity Phase 2 we just built. The decision points are **placement, dose, and what gets cut to make room.**

Here's how I'd integrate it without compromising the lifting block.

## 1. Where It Goes

| Tue | Upper Strength | Optional Z2 30 min PM |

**The HIIT day replaces the Wednesday interval session — it doesn't add a sixth training day.** Adding a true HIIT session on top of four hard lifts and existing Z2 work would push total weekly stress past what the surplus and sleep can recover from, especially in Weeks 6–7.

|-----|---------|--------|

**Why Wednesday:**
- Maximum separation from lower-body lifts (48 hrs after Mon, 24+ hrs before Thu)
- Fully recovered nervous system mid-week
- The Thursday lower hypertrophy session is the most affected, so HIIT modality choice matters (see §3)

**Why not weekends:** Sat Z2 is high-value for recovery and adherence (outdoor, enjoyable). Cramming HIIT in there compromises both Sat and the start of the next training week.

---

## 2. HIIT Definition for This Programme

True HIIT means **≥90% HRmax** during work intervals, RPE 9, repeatable but uncomfortable. This is harder than the original "intervals" prescription, which sat closer to RPE 7–8.

- **Work intervals:** 20 sec – 2 min depending on format
- **Work:rest ratio:** 1:1 to 1:3
- **Total work time:** **8–15 min** (not including warm-up/cool-down)
- **Total session length:** 25–35 min
- **Frequency:** **1× per week, never more during this block**

Going beyond this dose interferes with lifting recovery and provides diminishing returns for the health adaptations we want.

---

## 3. Modality Choice — Non-Negotiable

The HIIT session must use **low-impact, low-eccentric modalities** to protect Thursday's lower session. In order of preference:

1. **Assault bike / Air bike** — best option; full body, zero eccentric load
2. **Rower** — excellent; mostly concentric, full body
3. **Watt bike / spin bike** — good; quad-dominant but no impact
4. **Ski erg** — good; upper-body biased, spares legs entirely
5. **Incline treadmill walk-to-run intervals** — acceptable, but more leg cost

**Avoid for this block:**
- Sprinting (high eccentric load, hamstring risk, lingers into Thursday)
- Hill sprints
- Plyometric circuits
- Anything with jumping, bounding, or heavy deceleration

---

## 4. HIIT Session Options

Rotate one of these per week. All include 5 min ramp warm-up and 5 min cool-down.

**Option A — Classic 30:30 (Assault bike or rower)**
- 10 × 30 sec hard (RPE 9) / 30 sec easy
- Total work: 5 min / Total session: ~20 min
- Best entry point; use Week 5

**Option B — 40:20 (Assault bike or rower)**
- 8 × 40 sec hard (RPE 9) / 20 sec easy
- Total work: ~5 min / Total session: ~20 min
- Higher density; use Week 6

**Option C — Tabata variant (Bike)**
- 2 blocks of 8 × 20 sec hard / 10 sec easy, 3 min rest between blocks
- Total work: ~5.5 min / Total session: ~22 min
- Brutal but short; use Week 7 *only if* readiness is high

**Option D — Norwegian 4×4 (Bike or rower)**
- 4 × 4 min @ RPE 8.5–9 / 3 min easy
- Total work: 16 min / Total session: ~35 min
- Best for VO₂max; **do not use in Week 7** — too much accumulated stress with the peak strength week

**Option E — 1:1 minute intervals (Bike or rower)**
- 6 × 1 min hard (RPE 9) / 1 min easy
- Total work: 6 min / Total session: ~22 min
- Good middle ground; flexible week

---

## 5. Phase-by-Phase Prescription

**Phase 1 — Accumulation (Weeks 1–4):**
- HIIT 1×/week, Wed
- Use Options A or B
- Skip in Week 4 deload (replace with Z2 30 min)

**Phase 2 Revised — Intensification (Weeks 5–8):**
- Week 5: Option A (re-entry)
- Week 6: Option B or D
- Week 7: Option A or E — **shorter, sharper, lower total volume**; this is the peak strength week, do not overreach on cardio
- Week 8: **No HIIT.** Z2 30 min only. The deload must deload everything.

**Phase 3 — Realisation (Weeks 9–11):**
- Week 9: Option A
- Week 10: Option A or E
- Week 11: **No HIIT.** Final push toward Week 12 test.

**Week 12 — Taper/Test:**
- No HIIT. Z2 walking only.

---

## 6. Rules That Don't Bend

1. **One HIIT session per week. Maximum.** More is worse, not better, in this context.
2. **Wednesday only.** Moving it to a lifting day compromises lifting; moving it to Sat compromises the next week.
3. **No HIIT in Weeks 4, 8, 11, or 12.** Deloads and tapers must include cardio.
4. **Fuel it.** 40–60 g carbs in the 90 min before, water + electrolytes during.
5. **If readiness <6/10 on Wednesday morning, downgrade to Z2 30 min.** No exceptions. A poorly executed HIIT session at RPE 7 is just expensive Z2.
6. **Track output, not just time.** Average watts (bike), average split (rower), or distance covered should trend up week-to-week at the same RPE. If output drops two weeks running, fatigue is accumulating — pull back.

---

## 7. Nutrition Adjustment for HIIT Day

Wednesday is now a moderate-stress training day, not a rest day. Adjust accordingly:

- **Calories:** Match training day target (~2,500 kcal for the 65 kg example client), not rest day
- **Carbs:** ~5 g/kg, with 40–60 g concentrated in the pre-HIIT meal
- **Post-HIIT:** 30 g protein + 50 g carbs within ~60 min
- **Hydration:** +500 ml on top of baseline, plus electrolytes (sodium 1 g) for the session itself

---

## 8. Monitoring Additions

Two metrics to layer onto the existing weekly check-in:

1. **HIIT output (watts/split/distance):** Should trend up at fixed RPE through Weeks 5–7, dip in Week 8 deload, recover and trend up again Weeks 9–10.
2. **Thursday lower session quality:** If Thursday's bar speed, reps, or RPE compliance is degrading week-on-week, HIIT is bleeding into lifting recovery. Pull HIIT volume back by ~30% (e.g., 10 rounds → 7 rounds) before considering removing it.

---

This gives her one genuinely high-intensity cardio session per week — enough to deliver the VO₂max, mitochondrial, and cardiovascular adaptations that distinguish HIIT from steady-state work — while protecting the lifting block that's the primary driver of body composition change. The Wednesday slot, the modality restrictions, and the deload-week omissions are the three guardrails that make it sustainable across all 12 weeks.

## Rules That Apply to Both Options

These are non-negotiable for plyometric work in a hypertrophy/strength block. Plyos punish carelessness more than any other modality in this programme.

1. **Quality > quantity.** When ground contact time slows, jumps lose height, or landings get sloppy, the session ends. No "grinding through" plyos.
2. **Low volume, high intent.** 3 reps is the standard set length for true power expression. Beyond ~5 reps it's a conditioning drill, not a power drill.
3. **Full recovery between sets.** 60–90 s minimum. If she's breathing hard between sets, she's training capacity, not power.
4. **No plyos in deload weeks (4, 8) or test week (12).**
5. **No plyos within 48 hrs of a max-effort lower session.** Option 1 handles this automatically (power → strength on the same day); Option 2 has to be monitored.
6. **Surface matters.** Soft enough to absorb landings (gym floor, rubber tile — not concrete), firm enough to push off (not crash mats).
7. **Landings before takeoffs.** Weeks 1–2 prioritise teaching/refining landing mechanics. A client who lands well won't get hurt; a client who jumps well but lands badly will.
8. **If readiness <6/10, drop to 50% volume or skip.** Plyos done fatigued are the highest injury-risk session in the programme.

## Phase-Specific Notes

**Phase 1:** Power work is teaching and grooving. Don't expect or chase performance metrics — landing quality is the only KPI.

**Phase 2 (revised):** This is where it gets dicey. Week 7 has heavy strength work, HIIT, plyos, four lifting sessions, and a calorie surplus that must hold. **If anything is going to crack, it's here.** Pre-empt by:
- Capping plyo volume at the prescribed level — no "I felt good, did extra"
- Watching jump height/output as the leading indicator (drops first, before strength does)
- Pulling plyos entirely from Week 7 if Week 6 showed any signs of accumulated fatigue (resting HR up, sleep down, bar speed off)

**Phase 3:** Power transfer to the main lifts should be visible — bar speed off the floor in deadlift, out of the hole in squat, off the chest in bench. This is where plyos pay off for a strength test.

**Week 12:** No plyos. Power is expressed through the test lifts themselves.

# 1RM Test — End of Phase 3 (Week 12)

The existing Week 12 outline had "heavy 3RM or 1RM" as a trainer's-call option. With Phase 2 intensified, plyos and HIIT added, and a good responder pushing genuine numbers, a proper 1RM test is now well-earned. Here's a full prescription.

**Test dates:** Mon 17 Aug – Fri 21 Aug 2026
**Lifts tested:** Back squat, bench press, conventional deadlift
**Optional secondary test:** Overhead press (3RM, not 1RM — see §6)

---

## 1. The Week Around the Test

The lead-up matters as much as the test day itself. Week 11 (Aug 10–16) is already a peak week — the prescription holds, but with one adjustment: **drop plyos from Friday's session.** Three full days of CNS rest before testing is the floor.

### Week 11 (Aug 10–16) — Final loading week

As prescribed: 3×2 @ RPE 9 on squat and bench, 2×2 @ RPE 9 on deadlift. **No plyos Friday. No HIIT Wednesday — replace with Z2 30 min.** This is the last chance to apply heavy stress; from Saturday onward, the only job is to dissipate fatigue while preserving fitness.

### Week 12 (Aug 17–23) — Taper and test

| Day | Session | Purpose |
|-----|---------|---------|
| Sat Aug 15 | Z2 30 min, light | Active recovery |
| Sun Aug 16 | Full rest | Sleep priority — 9+ hrs target |
| **Mon Aug 17** | **Squat 1RM test** | Primary lift 1 |
| Tue Aug 18 | Full rest OR 20 min Z2 walk | Recovery |
| **Wed Aug 19** | **Bench 1RM test** | Primary lift 2 |
| Thu Aug 20 | Full rest OR 20 min Z2 walk | Recovery |
| **Fri Aug 21** | **Deadlift 1RM test** | Primary lift 3 |
| Sat Aug 22 | Full rest | — |
| Sun Aug 23 | Optional 30 min easy Z2, mobility | Transition to next block |

**Why this order:**
- Squat first — most technically demanding, highest CNS cost, deserves the freshest day
- Bench second — completely different musculature, recovers well from Monday
- Deadlift last — accumulates the most systemic fatigue, so it's at the end where any residual cost doesn't matter

**Why a day between each test:** True 1RM attempts cost ~48 hrs of CNS recovery for a recreational lifter. Back-to-back days risk a sub-maximal expression on the second lift, which makes the test data meaningless. The dedicated day off in between is non-negotiable.

**Why no HIIT, no plyos, no accessory hypertrophy work all week:** Anything that adds fatigue or muscle damage degrades the test. The goal of Week 12 is to **show what's in the tank**, not put more in.

---

## 2. Estimating Opening Numbers

To plan warm-up sets, we need a working 1RM estimate going in. Use whichever data is cleanest:

**Primary method — Epley formula from Week 7 RPE 9 doubles:**
- 1RM ≈ weight × (1 + reps/30)
- E.g., 80 kg × 2 @ RPE 9 → estimated 1RM ≈ 80 × 1.07 = **86 kg** (RPE 9 = ~1 RIR, so true 1RM is closer to 88–90 kg)

**Cross-check — Week 11 RPE 9 doubles:**
- Should land within ~2 kg of the Epley estimate from Week 7
- If Week 11 numbers were significantly higher, use those

**Plan the test day target as ~5% above the estimate** to leave room for a genuine PR while keeping attempts realistic. Better to need a fourth attempt than to bomb out on a too-ambitious opener.

---

## 3. Test Day Protocol — Each Lift

Each test session takes ~75–90 min. Same protocol for all three lifts.

### Pre-session

- **Sleep:** 8+ hrs the night before
- **Food:** Normal training-day breakfast 2.5–3 hrs prior (~600 kcal, ~80 g carbs, 30 g protein, moderate fat)
- **Pre-lift:** 30 g carbs + 200 ml water 45 min before; caffeine 3–5 mg/kg 30 min before if she uses it
- **Hydration:** 500 ml water + 1 g sodium across the 2 hrs pre-session
- **Mental:** No new music, no new shoes, no new belt. Everything about the session should be familiar.

### Warm-up structure

10 min general (bike or row easy), then mobility specific to the lift (5 min), then the bar work below. **Estimated 1RM = E1RM.**

| Set | Load | Reps | Rest |
|-----|------|------|------|
| 1 | Empty bar | 8–10 | 60 s |
| 2 | 40% E1RM | 5 | 90 s |
| 3 | 55% E1RM | 3 | 2 min |
| 4 | 70% E1RM | 2 | 3 min |
| 5 | 80% E1RM | 1 | 3 min |
| 6 | 88% E1RM | 1 | 4 min |
| **Opener** | **92% E1RM** | **1** | **4–5 min** |
| **2nd attempt** | **97–100% E1RM** | **1** | **4–5 min** |
| **3rd attempt** | **102–105% E1RM (PR)** | **1** | **4–5 min** |
| Optional 4th | +1–2 kg from 3rd | 1 | — |

**Attempt selection rules:**
- **Opener (92%):** Must be a lift she could do for a clean double. If she can't, she's not warmed up enough — add another set at 85%.
- **2nd attempt:** Based on bar speed of the opener. Crisp → +5–7%. Moderate → +3–5%. Slow → +2 kg only.
- **3rd attempt:** Based on bar speed of the 2nd. Same logic. PR territory.
- **4th attempt:** Only if the 3rd flew up. Many lifters leave their best lift on the platform by stopping at three; many also bomb a fourth they shouldn't have taken. Trainer's call based on bar speed.

### Spotting and safety

- **Squat:** Safety pins set at depth, two spotters (one each side) or a competent single spotter on the bar. No spotters on a low bar with hands on her — they're there to dump the bar to the pins if needed.
- **Bench:** One competent spotter, hands hovering, lift-off used. Safety arms on the rack at chest height.
- **Deadlift:** No spotters. If the lift fails, drop it. Plates and platform must be appropriate.

### Form rules — when a lift counts

Define this **before** the test, not after. A 1RM that wouldn't pass at a competition is fine for general progress tracking, but the same standard must be applied across all three lifts and across future retests, or the data is noise.

- **Squat:** Hip crease below top of knee. No collapse forward, no dive. Stand up controlled, rack the bar.
- **Bench:** Bar touches chest, pause not required but no bounce. Even press, both shoulders stay down, no hips off bench (gym standard, not strict IPF).
- **Deadlift:** Lockout = knees and hips fully extended, shoulders back. No hitching, no ramping. Controlled return (not a dropped rep — unless platform allows).

If a rep doesn't meet standard, it doesn't count, regardless of whether the bar moved. Be honest in the moment — the goal is real data.

---

## 4. What to Record

For each lift, record:

1. **1RM achieved (kg)**
2. **Estimated 1RM at programme start** (from Week 1 RPE 7 working sets, Epley)
3. **Absolute change (kg) and % change**
4. **Bar speed on top set** (video if possible — useful for comparing to Week 7 footage)
5. **Bodyweight on test morning** (compare to Week 1 baseline)
6. **Subjective rating** — how much was left in the tank? (RPE 9.5? True max? Sandbagged?)

Sample expected gains for a recreational female lifter in a 12-week dedicated block with good adherence and surplus:
- **Squat:** +10–20%
- **Bench:** +5–12%
- **Deadlift:** +8–15%

Bench gains run smaller in absolute and relative terms — this is normal, not a failure of the programme.

---

## 5. Decision Tree — What Counts as Success

Define this before the test so the result isn't interpreted emotionally:

**Clear success:**
- All three lifts up by ≥ the lower bound of expected range
- Bodyweight up 1–1.5 kg
- Waist not significantly up
- Bar speed sharp on top attempts

**Mixed result — diagnose:**
- Some lifts up, others flat/down → likely technical or recovery issue on the flat lift, not a programme failure
- All lifts up but small gains → check adherence (sleep, food, missed sessions). Programme may have under-delivered surplus or volume
- Bodyweight up much more than expected → surplus was too aggressive; tighten for next block

**Concerning:**
- Lifts down across the board → over-reach not fully recovered (taper insufficient), illness, or major life-stress confound
- Bench up, squat/deadlift down → likely lower-body fatigue from plyos + HIIT layering; reduce conditioning in next block

---

## 6. Overhead Press — 3RM, Not 1RM

OHP was a secondary lift in the programme, never trained at true low reps. Testing a 1RM on a lift that's only been trained at 3–5 reps risks misrepresenting progress (likely under-expression) and increases injury risk (limited heavy-single practice). **Test as a 3RM** instead, on a separate day or as the second lift of the bench test session if time and energy allow.

If included on bench day:
- After 15 min rest from bench test
- 3 warm-up singles to ~85% of estimated 3RM
- 1 working set of 3 at ~95%
- 1 working set of 3 at PR weight
- Estimate 1RM via Epley (3RM × 1.10)

---

## 7. The Day After

**Sat Aug 22:** Full rest. Light walking, normal meals, hydration. Expect significant DOMS, especially after deadlift Friday.

**Sun Aug 23:** Easy 30 min Z2, mobility, debrief with the client. Review numbers, discuss subjective experience, lock in next-block goals.

**Week 13 (Aug 24+):** Begin next block with a deload-style reintroduction week. Do **not** start the next block at full intensity — even a successful test costs 7–10 days of recovery for the CNS and connective tissue. The next training block earns more from a soft start than from a hard one.

---

## 8. Logistical Checklist

Run through this with her two weeks out (Week 10):

- [ ] Confirm test dates work — no travel, no major social events, no work crunches
- [ ] Lock in sleep targets for the test week (8+ hrs/night, 9+ Sun night)
- [ ] Confirm food on test days — no novel foods, no alcohol Thurs/Fri/Sat before tests
- [ ] Equipment: chalk, belt, wrist wraps (if used), shoes, knee sleeves — all the same as Week 7
- [ ] Spotters arranged and briefed on standards
- [ ] Video setup (side-on for squat and bench, side-on for deadlift)
- [ ] Music/playlist sorted in advance
- [ ] Plates available — confirm the gym has enough small plates (1.25 kg, 0.5 kg) for accurate attempt jumps

---

This gives a clean, honest read on the 12-week block: three lifts, three days, full taper, defined standards, recorded data. The structure is conservative enough that she'll express her real numbers and not bomb the test through fatigue or rushing, and aggressive enough that PRs are well within reach if Phase 2 landed as planned.

Worth flagging now: if she's never tested a true 1RM before, build in a fourth warm-up session in Week 10 where she takes a heavy single at ~85% just to feel the rack walk, the unrack, and the setup under near-max load. First-time 1RM testers often miss attempts not from lack of strength but from unfamiliarity with the protocol.

# Final 12-Week Strength + Hypertrophy + Power Programme

**Client:** 26F recreational lifter, COC-controlled (no cycle phasing), fully cleared, identified as a good responder
**Programme Start:** Monday, 2026-06-01
**Programme End:** Sunday, 2026-08-23
**Test Week:** Mon 17 Aug – Fri 21 Aug 2026 (back squat, bench, deadlift 1RM)

**Weekly structure:**

| Day | Session |
|-----|---------|
| Mon | Lower Strength (power primer + main work) |
| Tue | Upper Strength (power primer + main work) |
| Wed | HIIT (replacing original intervals) |
| Thu | Lower Hypertrophy |
| Fri | Upper Hypertrophy |
| Sat | Z2 cardio 30–40 min |
| Sun | Off (steps + mobility) |

**Optional PM Z2 30 min on Tue and Fri** if recovery allows — drop in any week where readiness scores are below 6 or sleep is short.

**Default loading conventions:**
- "Top set" = 1 heavy set at target RPE
- "Back-off" = subsequent sets at ~85% of top set load
- Rest: 3–4 min main lifts, 2–3 min compounds, 60–90 s accessories
- Plyo rest: 60–90 s every set
- HIIT and Z2 protocols carried week-to-week per the cardio section

---

## PHASE 1 — ACCUMULATION (Weeks 1–4)

**Strength format:** 4×6 @ RPE 7 → progressing to RPE 8
**Hypertrophy format:** 3–4×10–12 @ RPE 7–8
**Power format:** Block A — extensive plyos, landing mechanics focus
**Cardio:** HIIT Option A on Wed; Z2 Sat
**Nutrition:** +200–300 kcal surplus, 2.0 g/kg protein, 5 g/kg carbs training days

---

### Week 1 (Jun 1 – Jun 7) — Introduction

**Mon — Lower Strength**
- Box jump (soft landing focus) — 3×3 (60% volume)
- Broad jump — 2×3
- Back squat — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Romanian deadlift — 3×8 @ RPE 7
- Walking lunge — 3×10/leg
- Leg press — 3×12
- Standing calf raise — 4×12
- Hanging knee raise — 3×12

**Tue — Upper Strength**
- Plyo push-up (from knees) — 3×3
- Med ball chest pass (5 kg) — 2×5
- Bench press — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Pendlay row — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Seated DB shoulder press — 3×8
- Lat pulldown — 3×10
- DB lateral raise — 3×12
- Cable triceps pressdown — 3×12

**Wed — HIIT Option A (Assault bike or rower)**
- 5 min warm-up
- 10 × 30 sec hard (RPE 9) / 30 sec easy
- 5 min cool-down

**Thu — Lower Hypertrophy**
- Front squat — 3×8 @ RPE 7
- Hip thrust — 4×10
- Bulgarian split squat — 3×10/leg
- Lying hamstring curl — 3×12
- Seated calf raise — 4×15
- Cable woodchop — 3×12/side

**Fri — Upper Hypertrophy**
- Incline DB bench press — 4×10
- Chest-supported row — 4×10
- Arnold press — 3×12
- Cable face pull — 3×15
- EZ-bar curl — 3×12
- Overhead triceps extension — 3×12

**Sat — Z2 30–40 min** (cycle, incline walk, swim)
**Sun — Off**

---

### Week 2 (Jun 8 – Jun 14) — Add a rep/load

- All sessions as Week 1; **plyos to 80% volume** (box jump 3×3, broad jump 3×3, plyo push-up 3×3, med ball pass 3×5)
- Main lifts: +2.5 kg upper / +5 kg lower where Week 1 RPE was on target
- HIIT Option A again, push average output
- Nutrition and cardio unchanged

---

### Week 3 (Jun 15 – Jun 21) — Peak accumulation

- Plyos to full prescription: box jump 4×3, broad jump 3×3, plyo push-up 4×3, med ball pass 3×5
- Strength lifts: 4×6 @ RPE 8
- Hypertrophy: push to RPE 8–8.5, add 1 set to one accessory per body part
- HIIT Option B (8 × 40:20)
- Sat Z2 40 min

---

### Week 4 (Jun 22 – Jun 28) — Deload

- Main lifts: 65% of Week 3 load, sets reduced ~40% (e.g., 4×6 → 2×6)
- Hypertrophy: 2 sets per exercise, no failure work
- **Plyos: 1×3 each, movement quality only**
- **HIIT: replace with Z2 30 min**
- Sat Z2 30 min (shorter)
- Nutrition unchanged
- Add 1–2 mobility/easy sessions, prioritise sleep

---

## PHASE 2 — INTENSIFICATION (Weeks 5–8)

**Strength format:** Top set + back-off sets, RPE 7.5 → 9
**Hypertrophy format:** 3–4 sets, final set frequently RPE 9 or intensity technique
**Power format:** Block B — intensive plyos, true power expression
**Cardio:** HIIT carefully placed; no HIIT in Week 8
**Nutrition push:** +300–400 kcal surplus, carbs to 5.5–6 g/kg training days, pre-training carbs to 60–80 g

---

### Week 5 (Jun 29 – Jul 5) — Reintroduction at higher intensity

**Mon — Lower Strength**
- Box jump for height — 3×3 (80% of Block B volume)
- Single-leg bound — 2×3/leg
- Trap-bar jump (~20% BW) — 2×3
- Back squat — work to 1×3 @ RPE 8, then 3×5 @ ~85%
- Conventional deadlift — 1×3 @ RPE 8, then 2×5 @ ~85%
- Reverse lunge — 3×8/leg @ RPE 8
- Leg press — 3×10 (last set myo-rep: 1 set to RPE 9, then 3 mini-sets of 3–5 reps, 15 s rest)
- Standing calf raise — 4×10 with 2 s pause at stretch
- Cable crunch — 3×12

**Tue — Upper Strength**
- Plyo push-up (full) — 3×3
- Med ball overhead slam — 2×5
- Med ball rotational throw — 2×4/side
- Bench press — 1×3 @ RPE 8, then 3×5 @ ~85%
- Weighted pull-up — 1×3 @ RPE 8, then 3×5
- Standing overhead press — 4×5 @ RPE 8
- Pendlay row — 4×6 @ RPE 8
- DB lateral raise — 4×12 (last set drop set, ~40% reduction, to failure)
- Close-grip bench press — 3×8 @ RPE 8

**Wed — HIIT Option A** (re-entry after deload)

**Thu — Lower Hypertrophy**
- Front squat — 4×5 @ RPE 8
- Hip thrust — 1×5 @ RPE 8.5, then 3×8 @ ~85%
- Bulgarian split squat — 3×8/leg, last set AMRAP @ RPE 9
- Seated hamstring curl — 4×10, last set myo-rep
- Seated calf raise — 4×12 with 2 s pause
- Hanging leg raise — 3×10

**Fri — Upper Hypertrophy**
- Incline barbell bench — 1×5 @ RPE 8.5, then 3×8 @ ~85%
- One-arm DB row — 4×8/side @ RPE 8, last set AMRAP
- DB shoulder press — 4×8 @ RPE 8
- Chest-supported row — 3×10
- Cable face pull — 3×15
- Incline DB curl — 3×10, last set drop set
- Cable triceps pressdown — 3×12, last set drop set

**Sat — Z2 40 min**
**Sun — Off**

---

### Week 6 (Jul 6 – Jul 12) — Add load

- Plyos full Block B prescription: box jump 4×3, single-leg bound 3×3/leg, trap-bar jump 3×3 (Mon); plyo push-up 4×3, slam 3×5, rotational 3×4/side (Tue)
- Strength top sets: push to RPE 8.5; back-off load follows
- Add +1 working set to one hypertrophy movement per session
- **HIIT Option B** (40:20) or **Option D** (4×4) — trainer's call based on recovery
- Sat Z2 40 min
- Nutrition: confirm surplus is landing (bodyweight tracking 0.15–0.35%/week)

---

### Week 7 (Jul 13 – Jul 19) — Peak intensification (hardest week of the block)

**Mon — Lower Strength**
- Plyos: full prescription, but quality-gated. If jump height or landing degrades, end the block.
- Back squat — work to 1×2 @ RPE 9, then 2×4 @ ~88%
- Conventional deadlift — 1×2 @ RPE 9, then 2×4 @ ~88%
- Reverse lunge — 3×6/leg @ RPE 8.5
- Leg press — 3×8 (last set myo-rep)
- Standing calf raise — 4×8 with 2 s pause
- Cable crunch — 3×12

**Tue — Upper Strength**
- Plyos: full prescription, quality-gated
- Bench press — 1×2 @ RPE 9, then 2×4 @ ~88%
- Weighted pull-up — 1×2 @ RPE 9, then 2×4
- Standing overhead press — 4×4 @ RPE 8.5
- Pendlay row — 4×5 @ RPE 8.5
- DB lateral raise — 4×10 (last set double drop)
- Close-grip bench — 3×6 @ RPE 8.5

**Wed — HIIT Option A or E** (shorter, sharper — *not* Option D this week)

**Thu — Lower Hypertrophy**
- Front squat — 1×4 @ RPE 9, then 3×6 @ ~85%
- Hip thrust — 1×4 @ RPE 9, then 3×6
- Bulgarian split squat — 3×6/leg, last set AMRAP @ RPE 9
- Seated hamstring curl — 4×8, last set myo-rep
- Seated calf raise — 4×10 with pause
- Hanging leg raise — 3×8 weighted

**Fri — Upper Hypertrophy**
- Incline barbell bench — 1×4 @ RPE 9, then 3×6
- One-arm DB row — 4×6/side, last set AMRAP
- DB shoulder press — 4×6 @ RPE 8.5
- Chest-supported row — 3×8
- Cable face pull — 3×15
- Incline DB curl — 3×8, last set double drop
- Cable triceps pressdown — 3×10, last set double drop

**Sat — Z2 40 min** (easy, recovery-focused)
**Sun — Off** (sleep priority)

**Pull-back conditions for Week 7:** If RHR is +5 bpm over baseline for 3+ days, sleep <7 hrs for 3+ nights, or bar speed visibly degraded in Week 6, **pull plyos for the week and run main lifts at RPE 8.5 instead of 9.**

---

### Week 8 (Jul 20 – Jul 26) — Deep deload

This is a deeper deload than Phase 1's, because Phase 2 went deeper.

**Mon — Lower (light)**
- No plyos
- Back squat — 3×5 @ 60% of Week 7 top set, focus on bar speed
- Romanian deadlift — 3×6 @ moderate
- Leg press — 2×10
- Calf raise — 2×12

**Tue — Upper (light)**
- No plyos
- Bench press — 3×5 @ 60% of Week 7 top set
- Lat pulldown — 3×8
- DB shoulder press — 2×10
- Pressdown — 2×12

**Wed — Z2 30 min** (no HIIT this week)

**Thu — Lower Hypertrophy (light)**
- Front squat — 2×6 moderate
- Hip thrust — 2×8 moderate
- Hamstring curl — 2×10
- Calf raise — 2×12

**Fri — OPTIONAL**: light technique session at client's choice OR full rest
